summary: src/main.ts (4889 lines) is a single-file vanilla-TS frontend with NO framework: one global `render()` function rebuilds `#app.innerHTML` from template strings on every state change, then `createIcons()` (lucide) + `bindUi()` (re-attach ALL listeners) + `mountActiveTerminal()` run. State is ~40 module-level `let` variables (settings, terminalSessions[], activeTerminalKey, activeView, poolStatus, roomStatus, etc.) — no store, no reactivity. Layout: `.layout` > `.sidebar` (brand + terminal session list `.terminal-side-list`) + `main.workspace` > `header.topbar` (session title + big `.actions` toolbar of view-toggle buttons) > `section.terminal-shell` (swapped content: `#terminal` div OR one of 8 panels) > `footer.statusbar`. Views are an `AppView` union ("terminal" | "pool" | "limits" | "dashboard" | "kombai" | "discussions" | "history" | "room" | "audit") toggled by `setActiveView` (clicking active view returns to "terminal"); each non-terminal view has its own setInterval poll. Terminals: `TerminalSession` objects hold an xterm.js `Terminal` + `FitAddon` per session; sessions persist across renders because `render()` detaches (not disposes) terminal DOM elements and `mountActiveTerminal()` re-appends the active one into `#terminal`. Only ONE terminal is visible at a time (no split panes); sidebar items + (unused-in-layout but generated) tabs switch `activeTerminalKey`. Input path: `terminal.onData(data => invoke("write_terminal", {id, data}))`. Output path: single global `listen("pty-data")` routes by ptyId to `session.terminal.write(data)`; `listen("pty-exit")` marks session closed. `invoke`/`listen` come from src/platform.ts which is dual-mode: desktop = real Tauri IPC; remote/web = HTTP fetch to a Rust server + one WebSocket per terminal (`/ws/terminals/{id}`), both re-emitting the same "pty-data"/"pty-exit" events — so a chat UI built on these two primitives works in both modes. "Switch" = multiple `AccountProfile`s (separate CODEX_HOME dirs, optional proxy, per-account bypass flag); `start_terminal` is invoked with accountId + agentId + cols/rows + optional command (e.g. `codex --dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox` or `codex ... resume <uuid>`). Codex session UUIDs are captured post-launch (`claim_session_for_terminal` retries) and persisted in localStorage for resume-on-restart. Chat-like precedents already exist: the Agent Room view (`renderRoomPanel`: `#roomFeed` message feed + `#roomComposer` form with target select + text input + send button, 2s poll, auto-scroll-if-at-bottom) and the Discussions view (rollout history cards with resume/copy actions). All HTML is escaped via `escapeHtml`; no markdown renderer exists. Programmatic prompt injection into a running Codex TUI is already done via `sendLine(text)` → `write_terminal` with `\r` (used by Skill buttons).
keyFacts: No framework: full innerHTML re-render via render() + bindUi() re-binding every listener each time. A chat UI must either adopt this pattern (re-render + targeted innerHTML patches like #roomFeed/#poolRows) or be mounted outside the re-render cycle (like the .eh-bg background div prepended to document.body, which deliberately survives renders).

xterm.js Terminal instances survive re-renders: render() removes their DOM element from parent without disposing; mountActiveTerminal() re-appends session.terminal.element into the fresh #terminal div, then fits+focuses. Only the active session is mounted; others are kept detached in memory.

Terminal creation flow: createTerminalSession() builds Terminal+FitAddon and wires terminal.onData -> invoke('write_terminal',{id,data}); startTerminalSession() calls invoke('start_terminal',{id,accountId,cols,rows,command,agentId,projectDir/workspacePath/repoUrl}) where command is the auto-run agent command (codex + optional bypass flag, or 'codex ... resume <uuid>'). closeTerminalSession() splices, terminal.dispose(), invoke('stop_terminal',{id}).

Output arrives via ONE global listen('pty-data', e => find session by e.payload.id -> terminal.write(e.payload.data)) and listen('pty-exit') set up once in setupEvents(). platform.ts makes these dual-transport: Tauri events on desktop, per-terminal WebSocket (/ws/terminals/{id}) re-emitted as the same events in remote/web mode. A chat UI can intercept output at this exact point — but the data is raw ANSI/TUI bytes from the Codex CLI, NOT structured messages.

Structured conversation data DOES exist backend-side: rollout JSONL files per CODEX_HOME. Commands list_discussions (DiscussionSummary: title, preview, messageCount, totalTokens, cwd, sessionId/rolloutId), list_prompt_history (all user prompts with text+timestamp+sessionId), claim_session_for_terminal, copy_discussion_to_account, delete_discussion. A chat renderer could parse rollouts instead of scraping ANSI.

Programmatic input to a live Codex session already works: sendLine(line) -> write_terminal with '\r' appended; used by Skill buttons (#skillReview, #skillInterfaces) to inject full prompts into the running Codex TUI. This is the simplest bridge for a chat input box driving the CLI.

Existing chat-shaped UI to copy: Agent Room view — renderRoomPanel() with #roomAgents presence list, #roomFeed scrollable message feed (room/dm/system kinds, sender labels, escapeHtml text), #roomComposer form (select #roomTarget + input #roomText + submit), refreshRoom() 2s poll doing targeted innerHTML swap with 'atBottom' auto-scroll preservation. Backend commands: room_status, room_messages{since}, room_send{text,to}, room_enable/room_disable.

State = ~40 module-level lets; persistence = localStorage ('codex-switch-terminal.open-terminals.v2' for open sessions {key,accountId,agentId,codexSessionId,projectDir} + activeKey; '...workspace.path' for global cwd) + backend save_settings/load_settings for AppSettings.

Session resume: Codex rollout UUID captured after launch via serialized claim queue (claimSessionForTerminal, retries at 1.2-10s delays); on app restart restoreTerminals() re-creates sessions and starts them with 'codex resume <uuid>'.

Switch/profiles: AccountProfile {id,label,codexHome,projectDir,proxyId,bypass} — each account = isolated CODEX_HOME; agents (AgentProfile, kind cli|ide) choose the binary; per-account bypass flag appends --dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox; pool feature load-balances accounts as an OpenAI-compatible API (pool_start/pool_status).
Keyboard shortcuts: only F11 (fullscreen toggle) and Escape (close agents/new-terminal modals). Everything else is mouse-driven. xterm has focus otherwise.
Views polling intervals: pool 3s, room 2s, kombai 2s, dashboard 5s, limits 300s, discussions 60s — each started/stopped in setActiveView.

All dynamic text passes through escapeHtml/escapeAttr; no markdown library is imported anywhere. lucide icons rendered by createIcons({icons}) after every innerHTML write (i[data-lucide] placeholder pattern).

UI text is French; xterm theme is a custom warm-dark palette defined inline in createTerminalSession; styles in src/style.css; a decorative 'event horizon' background (.eh-bg) is injected once outside #app.

integrationPoints: listen('pty-data', {id, data}) in setupEvents() — the single stream of raw terminal output per ptyId; a chat view could tap here (but payload is ANSI-encoded Codex TUI output, not structured)
invoke('write_terminal', {id, data}) / sendLine(line) — programmatic input into a live Codex session; a chat input box can submit prompts exactly like the existing Skill buttons do
invoke('start_terminal', {...}) / invoke('stop_terminal', {id}) / invoke('resize_terminal', {id, cols, rows}) — session lifecycle commands

section.terminal-shell inside main.workspace — the swap zone where a chat panel would live (currently `<div id="terminal">` or one of 8 rendered panels); add a new AppView variant + render branch + toolbar toggle in setActiveView/render/bindUi
Agent Room pattern (#roomFeed + #roomComposer + refreshRoom targeted-innerHTML poll with scroll preservation) — a ready-made in-repo template for a message-list + composer UI

Backend rollout-parsing commands: list_discussions, list_prompt_history, claim_session_for_terminal, copy_discussion_to_account, delete_discussion — structured access to conversation history (titles, previews, per-message user prompts, token counts); the natural data source for rendering real chat transcripts instead of scraping ANSI
TerminalSession + persistTerminalSessions()/restoreTerminals() — session identity (key, accountId, agentId, codexSessionId) that a chat pane must share to attach to the same PTY

DOM anchors: #app > .layout > .sidebar (.terminal-side-list session list) / main.workspace (header.topbar .actions toolbar, section.terminal-shell, footer.statusbar); modals appended after .layout as .modal-backdrop > section.modal
src/platform.ts emit()/listeners map — where remote-mode WebSocket frames become pty-data events; any new event kind (e.g. structured codex events) would be added here for web parity
risks: pty-data delivers raw ANSI/VT bytes of the Codex interactive TUI — there is no structured message/tool-call stream in the frontend today. An OpenCode-style chat (markdown, tool cards) cannot be built by parsing this reliably; it needs either the rollout JSONL files (tailed/streamed by a new backend command) or running codex in a non-TUI protocol mode (e.g. `codex proto`/exec JSON), which is a backend change.

Full innerHTML re-render on every state change destroys DOM: a chat view with input focus, scroll position, or streaming updates will lose state unless it follows the app's mitigation patterns (targeted innerHTML swaps like #roomFeed, or mounting outside #app like .eh-bg). Any naive integration will feel broken.

bindUi() re-attaches listeners on every render; adding chat controls requires wiring them there (or event delegation) each render, and calling createIcons() after any innerHTML write or icons render as empty <i> tags.

Dual-mode transport (desktop Tauri vs remote WebSocket in platform.ts) means any new event/command for structured chat must be implemented in BOTH the Tauri backend and the remote server (src-tauri/src/server.rs) plus platform.ts, or web mode silently breaks.

Injecting prompts via write_terminal while the Codex TUI is mid-render can interleave badly (existing Skill buttons already accept this risk); a chat composer sending to the TUI must handle Codex busy states.
Codex session UUID capture is asynchronous and retry-based (up to ~28s of delays) and can fail; a chat view keyed on codexSessionId must tolerate null/late IDs.

No markdown/sanitizer library is present; everything is escapeHtml'd. Rendering markdown for chat requires adding a renderer plus XSS discipline, in tension with the file's current escape-everything convention.
main.ts is a 4889-line single file with ~40 mutable globals; the working tree already has uncommitted modifications (branch feat/agent-room) — coordinate before large refactors.
Only one xterm session is mounted at a time; a side-by-side terminal+chat layout must change mountActiveTerminal()/fit logic and the .terminal-shell CSS (fit/resize is tied to visibility).
